conclusion: Organic sheaths must not clip their seam or add an open inward anchor. Filled cross-sections, closed contour extraction and carried-center clipping preserve closure through repairs. Direction-locked wall identity survives height modulation and is checked separately from ordinary infill bridges. Use round printed bead envelopes and exclude unprintable loops before they can count as structural support; sub-width closed tips remain valid. The two supplied projects and the final normal Release native matrix pass exported contour closure within coordinate precision and actual bead-bearing checks; geometry-based rules have no printer-specific exceptions. Top-contact regions remain, while unsupported fringes may be trimmed. Exact old support paths, all-model guarantees and physical strength are outside this evidence. Completing bearing increases support cost: the newer project changes from 63.65 g / 4h 6m 47s to 75.35 g / 5h 0m 57s estimated output; all non-support extrusion totals remain equal. Concurrent final slicing measurements are not a controlled speed comparison.
scope: Verified current uncommitted source, source-bound normal Windows Release core/native/app builds, focused and broad native regressions, actual Release exports and live settings readback. HEAD is an anchor only. No publication or physical printing trial.
